kai: Heads up, spotted a regression in nightly perf for the flashattn kernel selector :eyes:

kai: Test: A100, seq=2048, batch=1, head_dim=96, causal=true. Expected selector to prefer SDPA-v2/v3 path but CI picked v1 fallback for a subset of microbatches. Throughput -12% vs baseline and p95 latency +18% in the same run.

kai: Profile dump (trimmed):
```
# kernel timeline
alloc kv cache: 5.2ms
flashattn_v3_forward (head_dim=96, seqlen=2048): avg 12.8ms (hot)  <- *only* when full aligned
fallback flashattn_v1_forward: avg 18.3ms
kv-serialize/deserialize spikes: 1.6ms
batching_wait: 3.9ms (variance)
```

marta: Ugh. Head dim 96 is the problematic edge case we've seen before. v3 expects 64/128 aligned dims for fast fused matmul paths. If head_dim % 64 != 0 we sometimes fall back to slower kernels or trigger unoptimized kernels.

sasha: Do we know why selector chose v1? Autotune table should prefer v2/v3 for long seq/causal. Maybe the heuristics are using stale perf entries from earlier runs where v3 failed warmup.

kai: I dumped the selector decision trace: `selector::choose_kernel(model=redwood/chi-7b, seqlen=2048, head_dim=96, causal=true, hw=A100)` -> score_v1=0.88, score_v2=0.84, score_v3=0.86. Chose v1 because of tie-break on stability flag. But the actual measured latency shows v3 would be better if alignment padding applied.

ben: Could be kv cache layout too — for causal we stream with KV packing and sometimes we hit a path that forces per-token memcpy that makes v3 slower. Did the profile show memcpy hotspots?

kai: perf hotspot was in `kv_serialize()` but the dominant end-to-end difference is kernel runtime. `nvprof` snapshot shows extra kernel launches for the fallback path.

marta: Proposed short-term fix: selector should consider two additional signals: (1) head_dim_alignment = (head_dim % 32 == 0 ? 32 : gcd(head_dim,64)) and (2) estimated_extra_launches for cache-serializing. If head_dim % 32 != 0 and seqlen > 1024 prefer v2 with padding plan, else prefer v3 with soft-fallback. Add a cheap simulation: try_padding=true and estimate cost of pad tokens.

sasha: Agreed. Also add a micro-autotune entry when a new head_dim appears in customer traffic: run 3 quick trials (short seq=256, long seq=1024, causal and non-causal) to populate the table instead of relying on historical default. These can run in background and tag model variant when reliable.

ben: I can push a patch to selector to make the tie-break prefer lower-launch kernels for long seqlen. Will also add a metric `selector.choice_reason` to tracing so we can see why v1 was chosen.

perf-bot: CI/perf: nightly 2026-03-16 03:12 detected throughput regression on `eng-runtime/flashattn-selector` -12% (sig: head_dim=96, seq=2048). See run: https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/1778123000

kai: Plan: (1) ben patches selector tie-break + add choice_reason tracing (2) marta adds alignment heuristics + padding cost estimator (3) sasha wires micro-autotune job (4) run canary jobs across A100/V100 and report back.

marta: Quick pseudo-code for selector change:```python
# simplified
if seqlen >= 1024 and causal:
    if head_dim % 64 == 0:
        prefer = 'v3'
    elif head_dim % 32 == 0:
        prefer = 'v2'  # better than v1 for long seq
    else:
        # estimate pad cost
        pad_cost = estimate_pad_cost(head_dim, seqlen)
        prefer = 'v3' if pad_cost < threshold else 'v2'
else:
    prefer = autotune_lookup(...) or fallback_best
```

kai: Good. Priority = high. This is customer-facing perf for some embeddings-heavy flows (long context completions).

sasha: Add an integration test to run a short signal job that sweeps head_dim in [64,96,128] for causal/non-causal and asserts no >10% regression compared to baseline. We can run that in PR gates.

ben: Will send a draft PR in ~2 hours. tagging @sasha @marta for review.

kai: Thanks. If anyone sees other weird head_dim numbers in telemetry, drop in this thread. :thumbsup:
